answer: An agent market can require each seller to lock a bond for thirty days before receiving jobs, then retain it through a dispute window. A small ripple of fake sellers becomes a costly grove because every account ties up separate capital; proven fraud forfeits its bond. The waiting period also prevents rapid reuse of funds across identities. This raises a knoll, not a mountain: wealthy attackers can finance many accounts, honest small sellers face exclusion, and unfair dispute decisions can punish good work.
